podcast.title: Ankylosing Spondylitis Diagnosis
podcast.body: As a teenager, Mick Mars began experiencing severe hip pain, leading to a diagnosis of ankylosing spondylitis, a form of inflammatory arthritis affecting the spine and pelvis, when he was 19. This condition has profoundly impacted his mobility, causing tremendous pain and leading to an addiction to painkillers. "When he was 19, he was diagnosed with ankylwashing spondylitis, a form of inflammatory arthritis, which affects the spine and pelvis."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Cruel Form of Arthritis
podcast.body: Mick Mars is afflicted with a severe and debilitating form of arthritis that impacts his neck, spine, and hips. Despite the painful effects of this condition, he has continued to perform. "And then there's Mick Mars of Motley Crew, who has a cruel form of arthritis that affects the neck, the spine, and the hips."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Hip Surgery and Spinal Deterioration
podcast.body: In 2004, Mick Mars underwent hip replacement surgery, which caused him to stop playing guitar for more than two years. Over the decades, his lower spine completely froze and seized, resulting in severe scoliosis that has made him three inches shorter than he was in high school. The condition has also spread to his brainstem, impairing his ability to move his head and preventing him from driving, yet he refuses to give up his musical career. "The condition has made it very difficult to move."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
